scope: English on-demand comparison across sixteen arXiv subjects and Physical Review A and B. The public Physics edition uses four arXiv subjects.
assay: An initial partition requires a source passage for each paper. Only groups of three or more reach a second reviewer. The initial blind check inferred the narrowest possible question and oversplit the calibration controls. In the revised check the second reviewer tests the first proposed topic as a hypothesis against the original titles and abstracts, without first-stage quotations, a draft synthesis or the later ranking. A second independently quoted partition can confirm the group, retain a smaller comparable subset, or separate all members. The resulting date-specific question is supplied to the summary model.
sampling: Dates and editorial sampling were fixed in the protocol commit before dispatch. Read five high and five low ranks per date without overlap when possible. Select three fully rejected second-stage groups and two first-stage exclusions per date. Rotate alphabetically by majority primary archive or journal and choose within a source by SHA-256 of space-joined sorted paper IDs. Require nine of ten passes in each of the high, low and excluded sets.

blind_calibration.failed_validation_reason: Each of the eight final model outputs omitted or repeated a paper number. The revised path retries this response once with the complete number list.
blind_calibration.observed_control: Four continuous-variable key-distribution papers report a secret-key rate under different protocols. The blind judge made four separate groups. It also split papers on reconstructing or forecasting an ocean surface wave from sparse observations. These known controls supported trying a common quantity across settings and replaying the source snapshot.
blind_calibration.interpretation: Recollection changed the input and candidate memberships. The later frozen replay is the controlled same-input comparison.

previously_read_groups.original_reason: The methods embed flow physics into neural models, but the targets range from solving flow equations to super-resolution and reducing seed-to-seed closure variation. Those tasks do not share one physical quantity or numerical objective. The summary describes the methods as a broad family.

confirmation_groups.question: How accurately can learned non-local or constrained closures represent unclosed turbulence terms in RANS or Reynolds-stress transport models, and how well do they generalize beyond the training regime?
How accurately do neural architectures with built-in structure (multigrid, spatial-physical coupling) predict or reconstruct fluid flow fields on unseen test configurations?
How much does a Biot-Savart-based activation function reduce velocity, pressure and vorticity errors of PINN solutions of incompressible Navier-Stokes relative to tanh PINNs?

previously_read_groups.original_reason: The common outcome is a secret-key rate for continuous-variable key distribution. The brief keeps the security model and finite-size assumptions attached to the rates; the full text distinguishes an experimental demonstration from theory.

confirmation_groups.question: What secret key rate does a CV-QKD protocol achieve, under finite-size or composable security analysis, over a fiber link in an experimental implementation?

How far can a CV-QKD protocol with a modified encoding or receiver scheme extend the positive-key distance or key rate, compared with standard direct-transmission CV-QKD, in theoretical security analysis?

previously_read_groups.original_reason: The common hardware is an FPGA. Neutral-atom control, generating controlled noise samples for evaluating decoders and tracking Pauli frames have different outputs. Treating a throughput test platform as part of an operational feedback loop obscures this distinction.

confirmation_groups.question: What end-to-end latency and throughput can real-time classical control hardware achieve for closing the quantum error-correction decode and feedback loop within timing deadlines?
How fast and accurately can an FPGA platform sample circuit-level noise to validate the logical error suppression and timing of hardware QEC decoders?

previously_read_groups.original_reason: The common question is when sparse wave observations can recover or forecast a phase-resolved surface wave field. The inputs differ by design, and the summary retains dependence on prior information.

confirmation_groups.question: How accurately can the spatiotemporal surface wave field be reconstructed or predicted from sparse measurements (ship motion, single-point elevation records), and how does nonlinearity and data information limit this?

editorial_cases.headline: Proven mixing bounds for quantum Gibbs samplers reach 1D chains and high-temperature SYK
editorial_cases.summary: Five theory preprints prove gap, MLSI or entropy-decay rates for quantum Gibbs samplers; each holds in a stated regime (1D, high-T SYK, bosons).
editorial_cases.question: What rigorous convergence rates (spectral gap, MLSI, or entropy decay) can be proven for quantum Gibbs samplers across Hamiltonian families and temperature regimes?
editorial_cases.finding: All five prove convergence bounds for dissipative quantum Gibbs sampling. The brief assigns the mixing, gap and entropy results to their systems and states the temperature and truncation assumptions.

editorial_cases.headline: Proposed photonic and hybrid protocols report modeled entanglement gains over baselines
editorial_cases.summary: Three proposals for fusion, remote preparation and repeaters report gains over baselines in models or simulations, not experiments.
editorial_cases.question: How much can a photonic or hybrid quantum architecture improve the success probability, fidelity or resource overhead of its entanglement-based quantum protocol (fusion, remote state preparation, repeater swapping) relative to a standard baseline under realistic loss and noise?
editorial_cases.finding: The three architectures target fusion success probability, the resources and fidelity for remote graph states, and repeater entanglement distribution rates. The abstracts do not give the same protocol benchmark across the three. The repaired brief separately attributes the predicted fusion probability, remote-state resource count and simulated repeater rate and fidelity. It identifies the gains as model results.

editorial_cases.headline: Off-resonant drive models match cQED Stark shifts; DIAL gates validated in simulation
editorial_cases.summary: A published model reproduces measured cQED ac Stark shifts; DIAL's linear drive-to-Z map gives typical >0.997 GHZ-gate fidelity in simulation (n=2–5).
editorial_cases.question: How accurately can effective Hamiltonians derived for off-resonantly driven mediator/qubit-cavity systems predict the resulting dispersive interactions and shifts (e.g., Stark shifts, Pauli-Z couplings), and how can drives be designed from them?
editorial_cases.finding: Each treats the accuracy of dispersive effective interactions against an underlying system. The brief attributes the measured Stark shift to the journal paper, the gate fidelity to a simulation, and the dispersive Rabi benchmarks to the general framework.

editorial_cases.headline: COMPASS LTE fits: methanol and CH3CN D/H rise with D count in low-mass protostars
editorial_cases.summary: LTE fits to COMPASS ALMA surveys show D/H rising with D number in BHR71-IRS1 and IRAS4A2; CD3OD is detected in IRAS4A2 but not in BHR71-IRS1.
editorial_cases.question: What are the deuterium fractionation levels (D/H ratios) of methanol and methyl cyanide isotopologues in low-mass protostars observed by COMPASS, and how do they vary with the number of D atoms and compare with other sources and with models?
editorial_cases.finding: All three quantify molecular deuterium fractionation in protostars. The summary distinguishes the species, cloud, and first detection, and reports the LTE and chemical-model qualifications.

editorial_cases.headline: Theory: how much quantum-battery charge is usable under trajectory, local or port limits
editorial_cases.summary: Three model-based theory preprints find usable work set by charger measurement, entanglement persistence or edge-mode filling; none report experiments.
editorial_cases.question: How much of the energy stored in a quantum battery during charging can actually be accessed or controlled as usable work under the constraints of a given protocol (stochastic trajectories, local or collective operations, boundary port)?
editorial_cases.finding: The first study controls the spread in stored energy over charging trials. The other two calculate work extractable through collective operations or a boundary. The short summary presents the first study as a result on usable work.

editorial_cases.headline: Simulated surface-code variants cut qubit overhead 4–30× via modularity or yoking
editorial_cases.summary: Simulations (not experiments): modular hyperbolic codes claim ≥10× fewer qubits, three-yoked codes 4–4.5× denser (SI1000), optimized hyperbolic codes 4× efficiency.
editorial_cases.question: How much can physical-qubit overhead per logical qubit be reduced relative to the standard surface code by high-rate surface-code-based architectures that retain planar or bounded-local connectivity (modular hyperbolic codes, multi-level yoked codes, geometry-optimized hyperbolic codes)?
editorial_cases.finding: The modular and yoked memory studies report qubit overhead or density. The periodic-geometry result increases distance at fixed qubit count and encoding rate. The headline combines these with a qubit reduction and conflates larger-code projections with simulations.

editorial_cases.headline: Cavity-matter mode splitting is controlled by local field, geometry and emitter coupling across three platforms
editorial_cases.summary: Three preprints show splitting set by local mode amplitude (magnon), predicted cavity geometry (graphene/hBN), and 36.2 vs 24.1 meV in hBN emitters.
editorial_cases.question: What magnitude of coupling-induced mode splitting (hybridization strength) is achieved between a confined electromagnetic cavity mode and a matter excitation, and what factors control whether strong coupling is resolved?
editorial_cases.finding: All three identify or calculate a hybrid-mode splitting. The brief separates the predicted graphene/hBN splitting from the local-field and emission experiments and gives the emitter-specific energies.

editorial_cases.headline: Theory proves large one-way quantum communication gaps, up to exponential, across three problem types
editorial_cases.summary: Three theory papers bound how far one-way quantum or entangled protocols beat classical or unassisted ones: exponential for some problems, quadratic for others.
editorial_cases.question: How large can the communication-cost gap be between quantum (or entanglement-assisted) one-way protocols and classical or unassisted protocols for the same communication problem?
editorial_cases.finding: All three bound communication costs for a quantum advantage. The costs and comparison protocols are separately attributed. A lower bound against randomized two-way communication also applies to a one-way classical protocol.

editorial_cases.headline: Simulated and projected spin-correlation sensitivity at future colliders, via decay analyzers
editorial_cases.summary: Projected, not measured: STCF tau-pair simulation, FCC-ee Λb→Λνν̄ and HL-LHC bW studies test decay-analyzer sensitivity to spin correlations and couplings.
editorial_cases.question: How well can spin-density-matrix and angular-distribution observables, with decay products as polarization analyzers, be measured or predicted at future colliders to probe spin correlations and new-physics couplings in heavy-quark or tau-pair systems?
editorial_cases.finding: The tau-pair study estimates errors on entanglement and Bell-sensitive observables. The rare baryon study projects constraints on weak couplings from decay angles, and the top-quark study uses spin correlations to constrain a different interaction. The common spin-correlation headline overstates what all three evaluate.

editorial_cases.headline: Learned estimators recover stellar, asteroseismic and EOS parameters versus reference methods
editorial_cases.summary: Three preprints test ML recovery against UltraNest, ASPCAP/APOGEE labels or synthetic and Kepler spectra, each under model-specific conditions.
editorial_cases.question: How accurately and efficiently can machine-learning methods recover astrophysical parameters (stellar atmospheric parameters, asteroseismic quantities, or neutron-star EOS parameters) from observational data, as judged by agreement with reference methods or catalogs?
editorial_cases.finding: The targets are a neutron-star equation of state, stellar atmosphere labels, and oscillation frequencies. The methods all compare estimators with references, but the physical outcomes differ. The text identifies the three benchmarks, respective samples and limitations accurately.

One paper detects an ionized phosphorus species in remnants, one gives a tentative FeS detection in Orion and one infers ionization rates and electron fractions in massive cores. No three share the same species abundance or measured ionization rate.

The common mechanism is deconfinement in compact stars. The actual results concern the accessibility of twin-star branches, shifts of radial oscillation frequencies, and an axion-dependent phase boundary and core size. There is no common three-paper measurement of one of these effects.

At least three papers provide stellar effective temperatures and surface gravities: the PLATO benchmark catalogue and the DESI and Gaia-ESO spectroscopic catalogues. Their methods and calibration roles differ, but the published quantities overlap. The separate isochrone study targets mass, radius and age.

A Josephson diode measures rectification, the amplifier optimization studies a pumped gain and reflection landscape, and the junction-chain study predicts linewidths and mode populations. The common circuit technology does not supply a shared outcome.

The studies concern a globular-cluster orbit, early-universe gravitational waves, energetic particles from the young Sun and compact remnants inside neutron stars. The physical systems and testable signals differ.

editorial_cases.headline: Engineered control pulses widen quantum-gate error tolerance, mostly shown in simulation
editorial_cases.summary: Experiment: transmon X gates stay >99.5% at 20% amplitude, 4 MHz detuning errors; 2–7-order infidelity cuts and CZ/spin results are simulated.
editorial_cases.question: How much can gate fidelity and robustness to control errors and noise be improved by engineered control pulses, and over what range of error magnitudes does it hold?
editorial_cases.finding: All four quantify the fidelity of engineered quantum gates under control errors or noise. The brief assigns the measured transmon tolerances to the experiment and the reductions in infidelity and other gate results to calculations.

editorial_cases.headline: Proposed ALMA2040 surveys aim to test gas-to-star physics at cloud scales in nearby galaxies
editorial_cases.summary: Four 2026 science cases argue current (sub)mm facilities cannot map cloud-scale, multi-line gas across many galaxies. They are forecasts, not new measurements.
editorial_cases.question: What do cloud-scale, multi-line (sub)millimetre observations of the molecular gas and star-forming regions in nearby galaxies reveal about how star formation and its feedback are regulated?
editorial_cases.finding: The proposals concern gas-to-star scaling relations, young massive cluster feedback, chemical inventories and gas flows across scales. The brief correctly labels them as forecasts, but extends the specific multi-line, cloud-scale survey requirement to all four.

editorial_cases.headline: Calculations tie bilayer twist and stacking to topology, layer response and SHG
editorial_cases.summary: Three theory papers ask how twist or stacking sets symmetry-allowed responses in Bi2Te3 slabs and MoTe2 and MoS2 bilayers; none report measurements.
editorial_cases.question: How does the stacking or twist configuration of a layered van der Waals bilayer control its symmetry-determined electronic or optical response, such as topology, spin texture, layer polarization or second-order susceptibility?
editorial_cases.finding: The common input is interlayer geometry. The outcomes are electronic topology and spin texture, layer polarization and second-harmonic susceptibility. In particular the MoTe2 paper studies an electric-field response in a given twisted bilayer. The short text attributes a study of variation in stacking or twist to all three.

editorial_cases.headline: Defining Widom lines above AdS black hole critical points via complex zeros and scaling
editorial_cases.summary: Three theoretical preprints construct supercritical crossover lines for Kerr-AdS, Kerr-Newman-AdS4 and 6D Gauss-Bonnet AdS black holes; definitions differ.
editorial_cases.question: How can the supercritical crossover line (Widom line) above the critical point of AdS black holes be defined and characterized, including its scaling near criticality?
editorial_cases.finding: Each study constructs or characterizes a supercritical crossover in AdS black-hole thermodynamics. The text correctly distinguishes the models, the Lee-Yang and spinodal definitions and the supercritical scaling analysis.

editorial_cases.headline: Axion models probed as dark matter, interacting dark energy and stable late-time attractors
editorial_cases.summary: Three theory preprints model axions as cold dark matter or dark energy, testing stability, gravitational instability and dark-sector coupling; none fits data.
editorial_cases.question: How do axion-like scalar fields (as dark matter or dark energy) shape the cosmological background and perturbation dynamics, including stability and interaction with the dark sector?
editorial_cases.finding: One study calculates a gravitational instability for cold axion matter, one predicts a dark-sector coupling, and another finds fixed points for accelerated expansion. They use axions but supply different outputs. The summary separately attributes the model predictions and identifies their theoretical status.

editorial_cases.headline: Vortex handedness and OAM set response sign: photonic experiment, two theory studies
editorial_cases.summary: One experiment and two theory papers link vortex handedness or OAM to lattice vortex chirality, transverse momentum and spin, and Floquet current states.
editorial_cases.question: How does the vortex handedness or orbital angular momentum (topological charge) of a light field or photonic lattice mode determine the sign and structure of the resulting vortex-dependent response, such as transverse momentum or spin, vortex chirality, or localized circulating states?
editorial_cases.finding: The photonic experiment produces a vortex chirality selected by the valley. The other studies calculate transverse momentum and spin or localized Floquet states and currents. The headline treats orbital angular momentum as setting a common response sign, including where it is the measured output or no sign rule is reported.

editorial_cases.headline: Strong Mpemba effect via slow-mode cancellation: model-bound results for detectors and holography
editorial_cases.summary: Three preprints show slow-mode cancellation in Unruh detectors (secular master equation) and a holographic probe model; the conditions differ by system.
editorial_cases.question: Can a state initially farther from equilibrium relax faster (strong Mpemba effect) by suppressing its overlap with the slowest relaxation mode, and what conditions allow this cancellation?
editorial_cases.finding: All three calculate when suppressing the slowest mode speeds relaxation. The holographic study also checks overtaking from higher excess free energy. The summary preserves the model dependence and distinguishes linear, nonlinear and detector results.

editorial_cases.headline: Complete O(g^6) hot SU(3) pressure reported to agree with lattice data
editorial_cases.summary: Full O(g^6) hot-plasma pressure is now reported, with lattice comparisons reported in arXiv:2610.23675 and arXiv:2610.23676.
editorial_cases.question: What is the weak-coupling (perturbative and HTL-resummed) thermodynamic pressure of a hot non-Abelian gauge plasma, and how accurate is it relative to lattice or lower-order results?
editorial_cases.finding: All three calculate the thermal pressure of a non-Abelian gauge plasma. The repaired brief distinguishes the two gluon-plasma calculations and their lattice comparisons from the supersymmetric model and its mass-prescription dependence.

editorial_cases.headline: Compact ansatz ground-state errors benchmarked against exact or DMRG references in three models
editorial_cases.summary: Three preprints report ground-state energy errors vs exact, FCI or DMRG references: classical stabilizer subspaces, H2 Mamba-QE, and Gross-Neveu circuits.
editorial_cases.question: How accurately can approximate ground-state energies of many-body Hamiltonians be obtained with compact ansatz or variational wavefunction constructions, as measured by error relative to exact diagonalization or other reference results?
editorial_cases.finding: Each benchmarks approximate ground-state energies against a reference. The summary assigns the H2 error to the molecular calculation and the large-system deviations to the transferred Gross–Neveu circuits and preserves the limit on fixed-accuracy scaling.

editorial_cases.headline: Entangled and nonclassical probes: QFI gains depend on scheme, noise and source model
editorial_cases.summary: Three preprints give different answers on probe-state advantage: N00N time delay, N-probe Ramsey bandwidth under white dephasing, and two-photon spectroscopy in a weak-emission model.
editorial_cases.question: How much does using entangled or nonclassical probe states improve the achievable estimation precision (quantum Fisher information) of a parameter relative to classical or separable probes?
editorial_cases.finding: The time-delay experiment compares two readouts of the same entangled state. It does not compare classical and entangled probe preparations. The other studies compare probes or sources. The brief extends probe-state advantage to the readout comparison even though the detailed paragraph identifies the two detector schemes.

Two abstracts address polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon emission. The companion fine-structure paper fits gas ionization, density and metallicity from different lines. The three do not report the same PAH response.

All three report stellar rotation periods in populations of cluster members. The large catalog includes other periodic phenomena too, but contains measured stellar rotations. The Lagoon Nebula and Hyades/Praesepe provide age- and population-specific comparisons. Splitting all three removes a valid observational question.

The XY study tests a thermal sampling algorithm against Monte Carlo thermodynamic observables. The quantum Hall and neural-wavefunction work concern variational many-body states. A shared neural approach does not give three comparable thermal or ground-state outcomes.

The studies estimate pulsed heat confinement, the electrostatic near field of an AFM tip, and dipolar extinction peaks. A shared electromagnetic modeling framework does not give three estimates of the same observable.

The papers cover distinct questions including a strange-metal transport regime, pairing and Hall-state competition, optical Hall response, edge gaps and collective modes. No set of three in this batch establishes a shared measured quantity or specific theoretical test.

native_sample_method: In monthly arXiv website listings for fluid, plasma and statistical physics, sort primary entries by SHA-256 of the versionless ID. Read v1 dates and take the first two in each held-out week. Compare the native APS Harvest article records for the complete dates by journal, DOI, licence, abstract and publication day. Current versions of indexed abstracts can differ from v1.
cost_method: Subtract the parent artifact ledger for a restored run. The ledger on a cold week is the initial charge. The total includes grouping, synthesis and recoveries. Two October 7 repair responses failed SDK validation before token usage was available. The ledger has no charge for either response. The provider cost for those attempts is unknown.
scoring: Read the unannotated headline, short brief and full synthesis of the final restored edition against the individual titles and abstracts. Score both the physical question and summary for each rank, and the decision to exclude for the other candidates. Reader corrections are shown in the downloads and do not earn additional passes. The sample describes two non-overlapping weeks.
source_citation_repair: On October 21 the source checker twice rejected a brief citing a 2012 paper referenced inside a supporting abstract. The repair keeps the three eligible sources and preserves the original article record, omits the outside identifier from model input, and validates the finished citations against the ranked evidence. On October 7 a different check twice mistook 33 in the APS evidence DOI 10.1103/r577-33dc for an unsupported quantitative claim. The revised check removes complete registered evidence identifiers from quantitative comparisons and continues to check ordinary measurements.
publication_decision: Keep the 16-archive, two-journal edition on demand. All three sampled sets fell below nine passes out of ten. The source comparisons cover the two named APS journals and three checked arXiv subjects. The next review should test both wrongly merged outcomes and comparable outcomes missed across differing study settings on independent weeks. The public edition continues with four arXiv subjects. Decide the total monthly model budget after field measurements, including ongoing live costs.
